_comment: Every version of every part that gets rendered for the portfolio.
Add a stage by adding an entry to a family's 'stages' list. A stage's
-> renders a Fusion export. THIS IS WHAT THE 'current' STAGES USE,
because Fusion is the design source of truth. Re-export from
-> pulls that file out of git history at that commit. This is how
the superseded versions are drawn, since they predate Fusion.
-> uses the OpenSCAD working copy. Only for a part that never made
it into Fusion, like the spacer the tray mount replaced.
'camera' is shared by every stage in a family, so the parts stay
comparable in size to each other. It is OpenSCAD's gimbal camera:
translate x,y,z then rotate x,y,z then distance. Raise the distance to
zoom out. Run with -WhatIf to list what would be rendered.

stages.name: plate_1_v1
stages.label: v1
stages.caption:
One piece, pipe sockets hanging
underneath. Needs supports through
every bore, and scarring wrecks the fit.

stages.name: plate_2_split
stages.label: v2
stages.caption:
Split into a flat plate plus three
bolt-on brackets, so every part prints
in its natural orientation.

stages.name: plate_3_spoked
stages.label: v3
stages.caption:
Spoked wheel instead of a solid disc.
Whole tripod drops from 160-207g
of filament to 84-109g.

stages.name: plate_4_final
stages.label: current
stages.caption:
Bore opened 124.5 to 125.6mm after
measuring the real pan-tilt base.
The tabs had been 0.25mm too tight.

stages.name: bracket_1_v1
stages.label: v1
stages.caption:
The pipe lock screw enters from the side,
where the taper has pulled the wall in.
That leaves 1.56mm of thread.

stages.name: bracket_2_final
stages.label: current
stages.caption:
Lock screw moved to a pad on top:
6.2mm of thread and room for a brass
insert with 2.9mm of plastic around it.

stages.name: clamp_1_v1
stages.label: v1
stages.caption:
Solid barrel and a flat jaw. Only grips
a wall it meets square on, and two of
the three legs never do.

stages.name: clamp_2_rib
stages.label: v2
stages.caption:
Jaw becomes a vertical rounded rib that
touches along a line. A line plus a point
pinches at any angle. Foot deleted.

stages.name: clamp_3_narrow
stages.label: v3
stages.caption:
Outer post narrowed to 9mm. A wall
arriving at an angle sweeps sideways
and a wide post fouls it first.

stages.name: clamp_4_final
stages.label: current
stages.caption:
Pipe lock moved to a pad on top,
and the jaw resized for a 6mm wall
after the thumbscrew calculation was fixed.

stages.name: tray_1_rim
stages.label: v1
stages.caption:
Curved tray with a rim around it.
The rim traps the item at exactly the
moment the tray is trying to tip it out.

stages.name: tray_2_saddle
stages.label: v2
stages.caption:
Rimless saddle. Sides curl up 10mm to
roll the item back to the middle, ends
curl down 5mm so it leaves cleanly.

stages.name: tray_3_final
stages.label: current
stages.caption:
The mounting boss stood 1mm proud,
a plateau where the item lands, and it
buried the bolt heads. Now capped flush.

stages.name: mount_1_spacer
stages.label: v1
stages.caption:
A plain 43 x 26 x 15mm block with four
holes. The tilt arm offers two holes 15mm
apart, so nothing lines up at all.

stages.name: mount_2_cap
stages.label: current
stages.caption:
A cap whose socket drops over the arm,
so the arm resists twisting, not the screws.
6mm plate, and it recentres the tray.
